chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from his grandfather Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, that Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Hamadani wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام, asking him about wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) in
the ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday, so he wrote: There is no wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) with the ghusl of the Day of Friday, nor any other than it.

key_terms.الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, specifically the Day of Friday
key_terms.غَيْرِهِ: other than it, meaning other ghusls besides Friday ghusl
key_terms.يَوْمِ: day, here referring to the Day of Friday

ai.seo_question: Does ghusl (ritual bath) remove the need for wudu (ablution) before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding ritual purity for salat (prayer), affirming that wudu (ablution) is not required along with ghusl (ritual bath) for Friday, nor with other ghusls. It is transmitted through a written question sent to Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام and his written reply.
